title: Population-scale immune multiome atlas reveals regulatory disease mechanisms
title_zh: 人口规模免疫多组学图谱揭示调控疾病机制
abstract: Most disease-associated genetic variants lie in non-coding regions1,2, yet mechanistic insights are limited by the lack of an empirical framework for characterizing the molecular consequences of regulatory variation. Single-cell molecular quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping3,4 connects variants to gene regulation but lacks the power and simultaneous measurements to trace mechanisms from chromatin to expression5. Here we show that population-scale simultaneous profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression across immune cells reveals regulatory architectures connecting variants to disease. From paired single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin-sequencing (snATAC–seq) and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) analysis of 10 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells in 1,108 Finnish individuals6, we identify 51,083 cis-expression QTLs for 20,829 genes, 338,100 cis-chromatin accessibility QTLs for 210,584 peaks, 119,094 putative causal variants and 593,765 peak–gene links. Variants completing chromatin-to-expression cascades show twice the disease colocalization of chromatin-only effects, with massively parallel reporter assays7 validating 10,428 fine-mapped molecular QTLs. At evolutionarily constrained genes, we identify multilayered regulatory buffering, in which chromatin accessibility changes occur with normal effect sizes, but transmission to expression is attenuated through weaker, more numerous enhancer–gene links. This reconciles why disease variants preferentially target constrained genes despite apparent expression QTL depletion8–11. Analysis using a massively parallel reporter assay7 confirms that this buffering acts downstream of the regulatory element, with constraint operating at the chromatin-to-expression interface rather than on intrinsic cis-regulatory activity. Our atlas provides testable hypotheses for over half of immune disease associations, illustrated by cascades at autoimmune loci (TICAM1 and RHOH) and Finnish-enriched variants (TNRC18 and IL21R). Population-scale simultaneous profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression across immune cells reveals regulatory architectures that connect genetic variants to disease.
abstract_zh: 大多数与疾病相关的遗传变异位于非编码区域1,2，但由于缺乏表征监管变异分子后果的经验框架，机制见解有限。单细胞分子定量位点（QTL）映射3,4 将变异与基因调控联系起来，但缺乏力量和同时测量能力，无法从染色质到表达追踪机制。在这里，我们展示了人口规模同时对免疫细胞进行染色质可及性和基因表达的联合分析，揭示了连接变异与疾病的调控架构。在1,108名芬兰人外周血单核细胞（PBMCs）中，通过联合单核染色质可及性测序（snATAC–seq）和单核RNA测序（snRNA-seq）分析1000万细胞，我们鉴定出20,829基因的51,083个顺式表达QTL、210,584个峰的338,100个顺式染色质可及性QTL、119,094个疑似因果变异和593,765个峰-基因连接。完成染色质到表达级联的变异其疾病共定位率是染色质仅效应的两倍，质量控制报告实验7验证了10,428个精细映射的分子QTL。在进化受限基因处，我们发现分层调控缓冲，即染色质可及性变化出现正常效应大小，但通过更弱、更多的增强子-基因连接传递至表达被抑制。这解释了为什么疾病变异尽管表达QTL似乎减少，却偏向靶向受限基因8–11。利用质量控制报告实验7的分析确认，这种缓冲作用发生在监管元件下游，约束作用于染色质到表达界面，而非内在的顺式调控活性。我们的图谱为超过一半的免疫疾病关联提供了可检验假设，并以自身免疫位点（TICAM1和RHOH）和芬兰丰富变异（TNRC18和IL21R）为例。人口规模同时对免疫细胞进行染色质可及性和基因表达的联合分析揭示了连接遗传变异与疾病的调控架构。
